transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, I've been having these episodes where I just eat a lot, and afterward, I feel so gross. I get really disappointed in myself, like I should have more control. It gets bad enough that I end up writing some pretty awful things about myself in my journal.
Do you ever try to make up for these episodes of eating a lot by doing something to counteract the calories?

No, I don't do anything like that. I mean, I don't try to throw up or take anything, or go crazy exercising or whatever. I mostly just... I just sit there and feel awful about it. I don't really try to counteract it, I just deal with feeling sick and guilty.
How often do these episodes of eating a lot happen to you?

For the past several months, it's usually been at least one night a week. I'll finish up my cleaning shift at work, buy way too much food on the way home, and just... eat it all in one stretch. I can't really remember a recent month where it stopped for more than a week or so.
Do you feel like you have control over what you're eating or how much you're eating during these episodes?

Not really, no. Once I start, it feels like I just keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically. Even while I’m sitting there thinking to myself, 'Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,' I just... I don’t actually stop. I keep eating until the food is completely gone or I feel too uncomfortable to have any more.
Do you ever eat large amounts of food in a short period of time without feeling like you've lost control?
No, not really. If I'm eating a lot like that all at once, it's pretty much always when I'm having one of those nights where I just can't seem to stop myself.
Do you feel guilty immediately after these episodes of eating a lot?

Yeah, I really do. Honestly, that's a big part of why I decided to come in. After those eating episodes, I just feel... so gross, and really disappointed in myself. I feel like I should be able to have more control over it. I usually end up just opening my journal and writing really awful things about myself right after.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

Um, no, not really. I mean, my weight goes up and down a little bit, maybe a pound or two here and there, but nothing significant. I haven't had to buy new clothes or anything like that. It's stayed pretty much the same over the last few months.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period, but without feeling guilty or disgusted afterwards?

No, I don't think so. If I'm eating a lot like that, it pretty much always ends with me feeling really guilty and just... bad about myself. I can't think of a time when I did that and didn't feel disgusted afterward.
Do these episodes of eating and feeling guilty affect your work, relationships, or other parts of your life?

Well, I still make it to my cleaning shifts and my design events, so I'm getting things done. But it definitely affects me. The next day, I usually just feel really distracted and ashamed. And sometimes I end up putting off my sketching, mostly because I just don't want to open my notebook and look at those awful journal entries I wrote right after it happened.
Do these episodes of eating a lot usually happen when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset about something?

Um, I'm not really sure. I haven't noticed a connection like that, to be honest. It doesn't really seem to matter if I'm stressed or just having a normal day. Sometimes I'll just be at home after work, not really upset about anything at all, and it still happens. So, no, I don't think it's usually because I'm anxious or anything.
Have these episodes of eating a lot happened more frequently over the past few months?

Well, for the past several months, it's been pretty consistent. There's usually at least one night every week where I end up buying way too much food after my cleaning shift and just... eat it all in one go. I really can't think of a recent month where it stopped for more than a week or so. It's just been happening regularly.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during these episodes?

Yeah, I do. It's like... once I start, I just keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically. Even when I'm sitting there thinking to myself, 'Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,' I don't actually stop. I just keep going until the food is completely gone, or... or until I just feel way too uncomfortable to eat anything else.
Do you often write negative things about yourself in your journal at times when you're not thinking about one of these eating episodes?

No, not really. I mean, I don't really journal at all, so I definitely don't write negative things about myself in one. I might get a little frustrated with myself sometimes, like anyone does, but I don't write it down or dwell on it unless it's right after one of those times I eat too much. But outside of that, no, I don't really do that.
Do you often think really awful things about yourself when you're not thinking about one of these eating episodes?

No, not really. Aside from the times when I've just eaten too much, I don't really have those kinds of thoughts. I mean, I might get annoyed if I mess up a drawing or something, but I don't sit around thinking awful things about myself. It's really just tied to the eating.
Do you often think critical things about yourself on days when you don't have one of these eating episodes?

No, I don't think so. I mean, like I said, I might get frustrated if I mess up a sketch or something at work, but I don't really sit around being super critical of myself on a normal day. It's really just when I lose control with the food that I get down on myself.
Do you think poorly of yourself for reasons unrelated to eating or your weight?

No, not really. I think... well, like I was saying before, it really all comes back to the food and my weight. I don't walk around thinking poorly of myself for other reasons. I mean, I'm just a normal person doing my job, cleaning the building and getting through the week. I don't have this big negative view of who I am outside of those times I lose control with eating.
Do you think critical things about yourself on most days, even when you haven't had one of these eating episodes?

No, it's... well, like I just said, I really don't. If I haven't had one of those episodes, I'm not thinking critical things about myself on a normal day. It really is just the food that makes me feel that way.
Are there any times when you think poorly of yourself that have nothing to do with food or eating?

No, there aren't. I know you've asked that a few different ways now, but my answer is still the same. I don't really have those kinds of negative thoughts about myself unless it's about my weight or after I've eaten too much. Outside of that, I feel pretty okay about who I am.
